body_ar:
من أحكام تأجير المنازل أنا عندي دار أؤجرها وأجرتها لشخص فهل يجوز لي أن أخرجه عنها عند نهاية الشهر وأؤجرها لغيره من غير رضاه

أن عقد الإجارة من العقود اللازمة التي تلزم بالمباشرة، فإذا استأجر الإنسان دارا فقد استحق هو غلتها واستحق مالكها أجرتها، فإذا كانت الأجرة حالة معجلة فهذا هو الأصل الذي لا اختلاف فيه بين أهل العلم الكالئ بالكالئ لم يحصل، فالعقد قد عجل حينئذ أحد طرفيه وهو الأجرة، أما الطرف الثاني وهو الغلة فإنها لا يمكن أن تؤخذ دفعة واحدة بل تؤخذ مع الأيام حتى يكمل الشهر، وإذا كانت الأجرة مؤخرة فبعض أهل العلم يرى عدم جواز ذلك لما فيه من الكالئ بالكالئ لأن الطرفين معا تأجلا، لكن جمهور أهل العلم يرون جواز ذلك لأنهم يقدرون بداية الأمر كنهايته، فالإنسان عندما دخل هذه الدار من أول يوم من أيام الشهر فقد استغل بعض غلتها فيلحق باقي غلتها للشهر كاملا بما استغل..
body_en:
Among the rulings on letting houses: I have a house that I let out, and I have let it to a person. May I remove him from it at the end of the month and let it to someone else without his consent?

The lease contract (ijārah) is among the binding contracts, which become binding upon being entered into. So if a person leases a house, he has become entitled to its usufruct and its owner has become entitled to its rent. If the rent is due immediately and paid in advance, then this is the base case (al-aṣl), on which there is no disagreement among the people of knowledge: the exchange of one deferred obligation for another (al-kāliʾ bi-l-kāliʾ) has not occurred, for the contract has in that case brought forward one of its two sides, namely the rent. As for the second side, the usufruct, it cannot be taken all at once but is taken with the passing of the days until the month is complete. If the rent is deferred, then some of the people of knowledge hold that this is not permitted, because of the exchange of one deferred obligation for another that it involves, since both sides alike have been deferred. But the majority of the people of knowledge hold it permissible, because they reckon the beginning of the matter as its end: when the person entered this house on the first day of the month, he has already enjoyed part of its usufruct, so the remainder of its usufruct for the full month is attached to what he has enjoyed..

flags.note: CRITICAL FOR DISPLAY. The answer opens by stating that a lease is a binding contract, which points towards 'no', then moves to a different issue — whether rent may be deferred — and breaks off. It never rules on eviction. A reader will take the general remarks about the majority permitting deferred rent as the answer to a question about eviction, which it is not. translator_notes: Qur'anic and hadith renderings in this file are interpretive translations of meaning, offered to carry the Sheikh's argument in English. They are not a substitute for the Arabic.

In the source, the answer begins with the elliptical particle 'anna ('[the answer is] that ...'), the Joomla fatwa template's standing form. The English drops the particle and begins the sentence directly; no content is added or removed by this.

The date shown by the CMS (27 December 2010) is a bulk-upload timestamp shared by every item in this range, not the date the Sheikh gave the answer. The real date of composition is unknown. See date_is_cms_bulk_upload.

EXCERPT ONLY. The published text breaks off mid-argument and the full material is offered as a .docx download ('taḥmīl al-māddah', 'download the material'). The English ends exactly where the Arabic ends. The download-link label itself has been removed from body_ar as a navigation element and recorded in source_download_link.

'The exchange of one deferred obligation for another (al-kāliʾ bi-l-kāliʾ)' is the classical prohibition of selling a debt for a debt. It should not be rendered as 'interest' or as ribā, which is a different category.
'Usufruct' renders ghallah — the benefit or yield a tenant draws from the property.
